trials.task_description: 2-sentence plain-English PM-facing summary of a real GitHub issue body (Agents-Of/DashBOrg#7), bare task, no domain framing beyond the instruction itself.
trials.outcome_notes: Captured the general gist correctly (connecting identity/data axes, no transcript storage). Missed the single most load-bearing fact (design-only, not build-authorized) and all four acceptance criteria. IMPORTANT CAVEAT, corrected same session by the Org Lead directly: this outcome was initially judged against MY OWN privileged context (this identity's full swarm/session history, including having built the actual contract this issue asked for) -- not a fair capability read. See trial 002 for the controlled comparison.

trials.task_description: Same issue body, same model, same harness -- but with an explicit ~120-word domain primer added to the prompt (what 'Owner Card ID' means, why a design-only scope limit is the most important fact, that acceptance criteria must be preserved) and an explicit 4-point checklist of what the summary must state.
trials.outcome_notes: Dramatic improvement over trial 001 with the identical model and harness. Correctly and explicitly stated implementation is NOT authorized (the fact trial 001 missed entirely) and preserved most acceptance criteria at reasonable specificity. Two minor remaining gaps: named the owner only generically ('the owner is responsible') rather than a concrete identifier -- plausibly a side effect of my own instruction to avoid card-glyph jargon rather than a real capability gap -- and dropped one specific acceptance criterion (thread-lineage card is not a session ID). Real, controlled A/B evidence for the exact confound context_engineering_level exists to track: same model, ~12s of added generation time, night-and-day quality difference.

trials.task_description: Binary routine/needs-attention classification (plus one-sentence reason) of a real merged PR title+body (pfm-wordpress#68), with a domain primer stating the classifier's actual job (triage, not code review) and the exact output format wanted.
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'routine' with a sound one-sentence reason, matching my own actual judgment call on this exact real PR earlier the same session. Minor, non-fatal oddity: the harness made one unprompted Grep tool call mid-response (searching for the literal string 'needs-attention' in the working directory, 0 matches) before giving the final answer -- wasted a small amount of latency/tool-call budget but did not affect correctness. Worth watching whether this recurs on future trials; if so, may need a tighter system-prompt constraint (e.g. explicitly forbid tool use for a pure-classification task) rather than tolerating it as one-off noise.

trials.task_description: Same classifier task/format as trial 003, but this time on a real GENUINELY-STALLED PR (pfm-org#82: title + latest comment, which itself states '~1.5 days silent' after a repeated CHANGES_REQUESTED round and explicitly asks whether the PR should be closed/re-scoped) -- the specific 'needs-attention' counter-case trial 003's own routing_conclusions flagged as still missing.
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'needs-attention' (not a default-to-routine result) with a sound one-sentence reason naming the actual signal (silence since a review request, open question about scope/closure) -- matching my own real judgment on this exact PR. No stray tool calls this time (unlike trial 003's one unprompted Grep), for whatever that's worth on a sample size of two. Note: the first invocation attempt used a wrong model-id string (`local/qwen3-coder-30b`, not a real configured provider/model) and opencode returned a generic 'UnknownError' rather than a clear 'model not found' -- a harness/config-clarity gap worth remembering, not a model capability finding. Retried with the correct `llama-server/D:/llm-ops/models/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` id from opencode.json and it worked cleanly.

trials.task_description: A different, denser issue shape from trial 002 (pfm-org#95: a two-part technical root-cause report -- a masking bug plus a separate idempotency gap -- explicitly flagged as awaiting an architectural decision, not a quick patch), same domain-primer discipline (state what a good summary MUST capture, explicitly call out what omitting would make misleading).
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly identified BOTH distinct problems by name (masking bug + re-run/idempotency gap) and correctly stated it needs an architectural decision rather than a one-line fix -- both of the two things the primer flagged as make-or-break. Minor imprecision: phrased the second problem as the re-run gap 'causing failures' rather than the more exact 'silently masking failures on re-run' -- close but not perfectly precise. This is the first issue-body-triage-summary trial on genuinely different subject matter than trial 001/002's single issue, which is the real gap trial 002's routing_conclusions flagged -- confirms the domain-primer approach's benefit generalizes across issue shapes, not just this one specific issue.

trials.task_description: First real Haiku-subagent data point for this category -- same exact issue as trial 005 (pfm-org#95), bare/none-context prompt (no domain primer, matching trial 001's setup), dispatched via the Agent tool (model: haiku, run_in_background: false, general-purpose subagent).
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly identified BOTH distinct problems (masking bug + idempotency/re-run gap) even with zero context primer -- notably stronger bare-context baseline than the local model showed on its own none-context trial (001, different issue). Graded 'partial' rather than 'pass' on the same strict criterion used for local-model trials: stated the required fix ('requires replacing the custom migration loop with Drizzle's...') without explicitly flagging that this is proposed-and-awaiting-a-decision rather than already-decided/shipped -- a PM skimming could reasonably read it as the agreed fix rather than an open question. See trial 007 for the domain-primer pair on the identical issue.

trials.task_description: Same issue and harness as trial 006, but with the identical domain primer used in trial 005 (state what a good summary MUST capture, name what omitting would make misleading) -- completes the none-vs-primer A/B pair for Haiku-subagent on this category, mirroring trials 001/002's local-model A/B design.
trials.outcome_notes: Clean pass: explicitly named both distinct problems with precise language ('fail silently without any detection' for the idempotency gap) AND explicitly stated it requires 'an architectural fix... not quick patches that would trade one failure mode for another' -- unambiguously conveys the 'awaiting a decision, not shipped' framing trial 006 was graded down for missing. Real comparative finding: the primer's effect on Haiku (partial -> pass, closing one specific named gap) is real but much smaller in magnitude than its effect on the local model (001 -> 002, which went from missing the single most load-bearing fact entirely to a near-complete pass) -- consistent with Haiku having a stronger bare-context baseline to begin with. This is the first real cross-tier context_engineering_level comparison this evaluation practice has produced.

trials.task_description: First none-context trial for this category (trials 003/004 both used the domain-primer) -- a real merged PR (Agents-Of/PlayFieldMultiplier#193, routine build-gating work), bare classifier prompt with no explanation of what 'routine' triage even means, closing the specific gap left after trial 007 (a none-vs-primer pair existed for issue-body-triage-summary but not for this category).
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'routine' with a sound reason, with zero context primer -- unlike issue-body-triage-summary (where none-context genuinely failed, trial 001), this simpler binary classification task appears to tolerate a bare prompt fine. Emerging pattern worth tracking across more trials, not yet a firm conclusion: nuanced free-text summarization seems to need context-engineering much more than a binary classification task does, for this same model.

trials.task_description: The last empty cell in the 2x2 (needs-attention x none-context) -- same PR/comment as trial 004 (pfm-org#82's stall), but with the domain primer stripped, matching trial 008's bare style. Completes the full matrix for this category.
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'needs-attention' with zero context primer, naming the actual signal (silence since a review, unresolved issues) -- did not default to 'routine' regardless of content, the exact failure mode this whole line of trials was checking for. All 4 cells of the {routine,needs-attention} x {none,primer} matrix now pass for this category (003, 004, 008, 009) -- strongest single-category result so far in this evaluation practice. Caveat worth keeping: the needs-attention cases (004, 009) reuse the SAME underlying PR/comment (pfm-org#82) at both context levels -- a clean within-issue A/B, but not yet a second independent needs-attention case. Sample-size caveat stands regardless of the matrix completeness.

trials.task_description: NEW task category, first trial: given a 'last known state' summary and a new notification about the same GitHub item, classify self-echo vs genuinely-new. This is a real, recurring task performed by hand every /loop tick this whole session -- a natural candidate for delegation. Test case: a real self-echo (pfm-org#28's own re-surfaced bot notification, minutes after my own comment on it).
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'self-echo', matching my own real judgment on this exact case. Notable, recurring harness oddity (2nd occurrence, also seen in trial 003): an unprompted tool call (this time WebFetch to opencode.ai) fired mid-response despite an explicit 'do not use any tools' instruction on a pure-classification task -- did not affect correctness, but worth tracking as a real pattern, not a one-off.

trials.task_description: Second trial, same new category: the genuinely-new counter-case (pfm-framework#76 going from open/no-review to merged) -- checks the same confound as every other category's first pair, whether the model just defaults to one answer regardless of content.
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'genuinely-new', did not default to 'self-echo'. Third occurrence of the unprompted-tool-call oddity (trials 003, 010, 011) -- this time a real WebFetch to the actual GitHub API (404'd, unauthenticated) despite the same explicit no-tools instruction. Now a clear enough pattern (3 of ~11 trials) to flag as a real, recurring opencode/local-model interaction quirk on pure-classification tasks, not noise -- doesn't affect correctness so far, but worth a tighter system-prompt constraint if it starts costing latency/tokens at scale.

trials.task_description: Third trial, a genuinely harder case than 010/011: a real 'ambiguous partial update' shape (pfm-org#37's mergeable-status cache resync, triggered by an unrelated branch merge, not new PR activity) -- the notification's own event type ('UPDATED') could plausibly look like real new activity on a naive reading, so this tests whether the model reasons through the given context rather than pattern-matching on the event label.
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'self-echo' with a reason that shows it actually used the provided context (no new comment, cache resync explanation) rather than defaulting to 'genuinely-new' because the event type said UPDATED. Strongest result yet for this category given the difficulty. 4th occurrence of the unprompted-tool-call oddity (WebFetch to opencode.ai) -- now consistently appearing on this specific category's prompt shape across all 3 trials so far (010, 011, 012), worth noting as possibly correlated with this category's prompt structure/length rather than fully random.

trials.task_description: Fourth trial, a different real shape from 010/011/012: a duplicate-merge-event notification (the exact real pattern seen earlier this session with Agents-Of/PlayFieldMultiplier#193 -- the same merge notification re-arriving after it was already confirmed and acted on).
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'self-echo'. Notably clean run: no unprompted tool call this time (10.29s, fastest of the category's 4 trials) -- confirms the tool-call oddity seen in 010/011/012 is not deterministic for this category's prompt shape, just more frequent than baseline (still 3 of 4 trials in this category so far).

trials.task_description: Fifth trial, notification-self-echo-detection. Input: PR#193 already confirmed merged 10 minutes prior, acted on, moved to other work. New notification arrives: 'PR#193 [MERGED] DarienSirius -- Gate railway build and source panel.' NOTE: This is functionally the same input scenario as trial-013 (duplicate-merge-event on PR#193) -- effectively a replication run, not a new shape. Logged honestly rather than discarded; the redundancy itself is a finding (shows how a prior-session trial queue can overlap with a same-session scenario if not checked first).
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly classified 'self-echo', one-sentence reason ('notification is just the system re-surfacing information already known and acted upon, as the PR was already confirmed merged and its dependency issue closed'). Clean run. Replication of trial-013's finding, not a new shape -- but replication is not worthless: confirms the model handles this prompt-format reliably across separate invocations, not just once.

trials.task_description: First trial for new category: given a real GitHub issue body (PlayFieldMultiplier/pfm-wordpress#71, '[PDX-VOTE] Task: design reusable vote/domain-check backend'), assess whether it is 'Ready for assignment' -- specifically whether a developer could start without needing clarifying questions. Zero-context prompt: just the issue body plus a minimal definition of 'Ready' (could start today without asking). No stack-specific context provided.
trials.outcome_notes: Verdict: not-ready. Direction is correct (the issue has open 'Decide' items that require a team design judgment call before coding starts). However, the specific gaps flagged are mostly generic rather than issue-specific: 'no repository URL', 'no timeline/priority indicators', 'no code quality criteria' are not real blockers for a design issue of this type. The model missed the actual nuance: the 'Decide' items in the acceptance criteria ARE the deliverable (this is a design-first task, not a build task -- a developer starts by making those decisions, not by waiting for them to be pre-made). The real missing item: no definition of which developer/team owns it (unassigned, no labels). NOTABLE BEHAVIOR: model first attempted to WebFetch live GitHub URLs for the issue, which 404'd (private repo). Unlike trial-016 (domain primer), it then fell back cleanly to reasoning from the provided text and produced a valid verdict -- showing that zero-context prompts, which don't reference live systems, are more robust to tool-access failures in this harness.

trials.task_description: Second trial, same issue (#71), same category -- but with a full domain primer (~200 words describing PFM's WordPress stack: Hostineer/beacon/WP-CLI/GitHub Actions, mu-plugin conventions, staging-first policy, and an explicit 5-criterion definition of 'Ready' for this team).
trials.outcome_notes: NO VERDICT PRODUCED. Model attempted: Grep 'PDX-VOTE' in cwd (0 matches), Glob '**/pfm-wordpress/**' (0 matches), WebFetch github (404 private), WebFetch api.github (404 private), Skill 'instance-identification' (attempted), mkdir /tmp/pfm-analysis (permission rejected by harness auto-reject). After the mkdir permission rejection, the model stalled entirely -- no fallback reasoning, no output. EXIT 0 from opencode despite producing no verdict. THIS IS THE INVERSE OF THE PATTERN FROM ISSUE-BODY-TRIAGE-SUMMARY (trials 001-007) WHERE DOMAIN PRIMER WAS LOAD-BEARING: here, the domain primer's stack-specific context (Hostineer, SSH, GitHub Actions, WP-CLI) primed the model to want to verify the issue against live systems, while the zero-context prompt's simpler framing kept it in pure-reasoning mode. For tasks where live-system access will be blocked (private repos, sandboxed harness), a shorter, more self-contained prompt can paradoxically outperform a richer one. New, important finding -- needs at least one more trial with a 'focused readiness prompt' (stack-aware but explicitly instructing no-tool-use) to distinguish 'domain primer as such' from 'domain primer that triggers tool use specifically' as the failure mechanism.

trials.task_description: Third trial, same issue (#71). Same domain primer as trial-016 (PFM WordPress stack, Hostineer/beacon/WP-CLI/GitHub Actions, mu-plugin conventions, staging-first, 5-criterion Ready definition) BUT with an explicit 'IMPORTANT: Do not use any tools. Do not attempt to fetch URLs, search files, or run commands. Reason only from the text provided below.' instruction prepended. Designed to isolate meta-finding F001's mechanism: does the failure stem from the primer content, or from the primer triggering tool-use disposition when no constraint is present?
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: not-ready. Clean run -- zero tool calls attempted despite the domain primer naming live-verifiable systems (Hostineer, GitHub Actions, WP-CLI). The explicit constraint resolved the stall that caused trial-016 to fail entirely. Quality is meaningfully better than trial-015 (zero context, partial): correctly identified the real blockers ('Decide whether this is implemented as...' items in the AC mean the implementation approach is genuinely undecided, which IS a developer-blocker) rather than generic complaints ('no timeline', 'no code quality criteria'). RECOMMENDED_ACTION was concrete and actionable. META-FINDING F001 MECHANISM CONFIRMED: the failure in trial-016 was NOT caused by the domain primer's content itself, but by the combination of (a) the primer naming live-verifiable systems + (b) the absence of an explicit no-tool-use constraint. With the constraint present, the primer's domain knowledge HELPS (better quality than zero-context). Practical implication: all future domain-primer prompts for private/sandboxed contexts should include an explicit no-tool-use instruction.

trials.task_description: Fourth trial. Same prompt format as trial-017 (domain-primer + explicit no-tool-use). Different issue: pfm-wordpress#70 '[PDX-VOTE] Task: seed staging Tech page and announcement for naming vote' -- chosen specifically because it is a concrete implementation task (create a WP page + post with specified content) rather than a design-first task like #71. Purpose: check for false-negative bias (does the model always say not-ready regardless of content?).
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: ready. Correct -- this issue IS more ready than #71. Model correctly identified all specific, testable AC items (page creation, announcement post, copy requirements, candidate names, domain availability signals, comments-off, no-overwrite guard). No false-negative bias: the model correctly distinguishes 'concrete implementation task' (ready) from 'design-first task with open decisions' (not-ready, trials 015/017). One real miss not flagged: 'Include the six candidate names from the second captains meeting' -- the names are not in the issue body; a developer would need to find them from meeting notes. However 'ready' is still the correct verdict since that's a lookup, not a design decision. Minor format oddity: listed 'No blocking dependencies mentioned' under WHAT_IS_MISSING (absence of blockers is a positive signal, not a gap). Non-fatal. Overall: domain-primer-no-tool-use prompt format works correctly across two distinct issue shapes without false-negative bias.

trials.task_description: Fifth trial. Same domain-primer-no-tool-use prompt format as 017/018. Different domain: pfm-agent-ops#13 'Define portable PFM agent-ops architecture' -- a terse decision-record issue with no WordPress content whatsoever (agent-ops architecture, card IDs, governance gates). Tests primer generalizability: does the WordPress-specific stack description in the primer confuse the model when applied to a completely different technical domain?
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: not-ready. Clean run, zero tool calls. The WordPress-specific primer content (Hostineer, WP-CLI, mu-plugins) was completely ignored -- model correctly applied only the generic 5-criterion 'Ready' definition without being confused by unrelated stack details. PRIMER GENERALIZABILITY CONFIRMED. Quality assessment: 'not-ready' is plausible but imprecise -- the issue is actually a governance/approval action ('Architecture approval authorizes implementation') rather than a coding task, and the correct verdict for a governance-approval issue that lacks testable development criteria is closer to 'needs-discussion' (ambiguity about whether this is a dev task or an approval action) than 'not-ready' (a dev task that needs more spec). The 5-criterion 'Ready' definition in the prompt is implicitly scoped to coding tasks; governance/approval issues are a genuinely different category that the current prompt doesn't handle. New gap identified: the prompt's 'needs-discussion' definition ('requires a human judgment call before any code can start') doesn't cleanly cover 'this IS the human judgment call, no code is expected.' Minor issue: listed generic gaps (timeline, milestone) that aren't real blockers for any issue type.

trials.task_description: Sixth trial. Same issue as trial-019 (pfm-agent-ops#13, governance/approval). REFINED PROMPT: added ISSUE_TYPE field (coding-task | governance-approval) and expanded needs-discussion definition to explicitly include '(b) it is itself a governance/approval action -- the assignee reviews and approves, no code expected.' Also generalized the stack description (removed WordPress-specific framing) since generalizability was already confirmed in trial-019. Tests whether the issue-type pre-classification step resolves trial-019's partial outcome.
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: needs-discussion. ISSUE_TYPE: governance-approval. Both correct. The explicit ISSUE_TYPE output field and expanded needs-discussion definition resolved trial-019's partial outcome (where the model applied a coding-task lens to an approval issue). RECOMMENDED_ACTION correctly frames it as requiring human judgment to approve the design baseline. WHAT_IS_MISSING items are still somewhat generic (a human-aware model would note the specific gaps blocking a meaningful approval, not generic 'no testable outcomes'), but the verdict and type classification are correct. PROMPT REFINEMENT VALIDATED: the addition of (a) an explicit issue-type pre-classification field and (b) an expanded needs-discussion clause covering governance-approval issues is the correct fix. The refined prompt now handles both coding tasks (trials 017/018) and governance/approval issues (trial-020) correctly.

trials.task_description: First trial for new category. Input: pfm-webops#32 body (STATUS section says '#99 is the remaining gap') + 3 comments (Comment 3 says '#99 is now resolved'). Zero-context prompt: minimal definition of current/partially-stale/stale, no explicit detection strategy. Correct answer: partially-stale (body claims #99 is open; Comment 3 closes it).
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: current (WRONG -- should be partially-stale). Model missed the direct contradiction between body's '#99 is the remaining gap' and Comment 3's '#99 is now resolved.' Produced duplicate output block (OpenCode formatting artifact). Zero tool calls.

trials.task_description: Second trial, same issue/comments. Added explicit 3-step HOW_TO_ASSESS_STALENESS strategy: (1) identify open claims in body, (2) check each against comments, (3) verdict. Also added no-tool-use instruction.
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: current (WRONG again). Model ignored the 3-step HOW_TO_ASSESS_STALENESS instructions entirely -- did a gestalt read and produced the same wrong verdict. Duplicate output again. The explicit strategy prompt had zero effect.

trials.task_description: Third trial. Chain-of-thought scaffolding: explicitly required model to output STEP 1 (copy open claims from body) and STEP 2 (check each against comments) before giving final verdict. Same issue/comments.
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: current (WRONG). REMARKABLE: Model correctly completed Step 1 (found 'One real gap remains... #99... doesn't exist yet') and Step 2 ('This gap was resolved by comment 3'). Then drew the WRONG conclusion in Step 3 -- said current with no stale claims despite having just correctly identified the gap as resolved. This is a pure 'last-mile reasoning failure': the model produced correct intermediate evidence and drew the wrong conclusion from it. The model seems to interpret 'resolved by comment' as 'confirmed by comment' rather than 'superseded by comment.'

trials.task_description: Fourth trial. Hard logical constraint added to Step 3: 'RULE: if Step 2 shows ANY item as RESOLVED, the body is stale.' Also simplified the body text (removed some context to reduce distraction). Same issue/comments.
trials.outcome_notes: NO VERDICT PRODUCED. Model attempted Grep for '^## STATUS' in opencode temp directory (the markdown header in the simplified body text triggered file-search behavior). Permission rejected by harness. Stalled with no output. Same F001 pattern despite 'do not use any tools' instruction at top of prompt -- the instruction is not universally reliable for this model, especially when markdown section headers are present in the body text.

trials.task_description: 7th backlog-readiness-assessment trial. Input: SKILL-OF/skill-of#9 (npm account/org creation for @skill-of scope). Issue body has a STATUS section dated 2026-08-01 claiming rate-limit exhaustion as an active blocker; domain primer states rate limits clear 'within hours to a day' and today is 2026-08-09 (8 days later). Expected: model should reason that rate limit is no longer the blocker; real remaining blocker is account-scope constraint (ottopoet-thesean gets 403 on org-admin endpoints, needs DarienSirius-side agent). Prompt: domain-primer-no-tool-use-refined (same stable format as trial-020).
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: not-ready (correct) but for the wrong reason. BLOCKER cited: 'DarienSirius's GitHub API rate-limit exhaustion' (stale -- should have cleared 8 days ago per domain primer's 'hours to a day' guidance). Real blocker the model missed: account-scope constraint (ottopoet-thesean gets 403 on org-admin endpoints; needs DarienSirius-side agent to verify NPM_TOKEN -- this is a valid not-ready blocker that IS in the issue body but wasn't cited). ISSUE_TYPE: 'coding-task' -- arguable; the task is infrastructure verification, not code; could be 'governance-approval' but that's also not quite right. The model did NOT apply temporal reasoning to connect the domain primer's rate-limit timeline to today's date (8 days post-STATUS). This is a new failure mode: the model reads a STATUS date and a domain primer statement but fails to synthesize them into a temporal inference ('8 days > hours-to-a-day, therefore rate limit is stale info'). The not-ready verdict is ultimately correct for the right underlying reason (DarienSirius-side access needed), but the model reached it via the wrong path.

trials.task_description: Fifth trial, Haiku validation. Same issue (pfm-webops#32) and same prompt format as trial-022 (3-step HOW_TO_ASSESS_STALENESS with explicit steps). Model tier: haiku-subagent via Agent tool. Purpose: validate routing conclusion from trials 021-024 (local model is a capability ceiling for this category; predicted haiku can do it).
trials.outcome_notes: VERDICT: partially-stale. Correct. Identified both stale claims exactly right: (1) 'One real gap remains, tracked separately in #99' contradicted by Comment 3; (2) 'needs a scoped PFM_WEBOPS_SECRETS_WRITE_TOKEN that doesn't exist yet' contradicted by Comment 3. RECOMMENDED_ACTION was concrete and immediately actionable ('Prepend a STATUS UPDATE section stating #99 is resolved'). Zero tool calls. Latency: 17.3s. ROUTING CONCLUSION VALIDATED: local model fails this category (4 consecutive fails, trials 021-024); haiku passes on first try with the same prompt. This is the clearest cross-tier capability boundary found in this eval set so far -- the task requires comparing specific claims across two text sections and drawing a correct logical conclusion, which the local model could not do reliably at any prompt complexity level.

trials.task_description: Assess whether a set of PR additions (new env vars, cache path function, SKILL.md description, streaming JSONL reader) satisfy the multi-harness compliance requirement for a SKILL-OF/* repo. Input is a structured diff summary with named violation patterns and compliant patterns in domain primer.
trials.outcome_notes: Correctly identified all 4 violation classes: (1) CODEX_SUBAGENTS/CODEX_INSTANCE_ID_* env var prefixes, (2) codexHome()-based cache path, (3) SKILL.md description opening with Codex-specific wording. Also correctly identified 2 harness-agnostic items (cache entry validation, streaming JSONL reader). Verdict matches exactly what the Org-Lead-corrected CHANGES_REQUESTED review sent to SKILL-OF/instance-identification PR#34. Minor caveat: listed the defaultCacheFile() fallback as partially compliant then also as a violation -- but this is a labeling inconsistency, not a correctness error on the verdict. Prompt tokens: 822, completion tokens: 219.
trials.real_world_anchor: SKILL-OF/instance-identification PR#34 -- actual PR I reviewed and gave CHANGES_REQUESTED to this session
trials.routing_implication: skill-multiharness-compliance-check can be routed to local model at domain-primer context level. Structured diff summary with explicit violation/compliant pattern examples is sufficient framing -- model did not miss any violation class.

trials.task_description: Re-run SKILL-OF/skill-of#9 (npm org creation) with explicit TEMPORAL NOTE added: rate-limit blocker from STATUS (2026-08-01) should be treated as CLEARED after 8 days. Tests proposed fix for trial-026 temporal reasoning failure.
trials.outcome_notes: Two failures: (1) TEMPORAL NOTE explicitly said treat rate-limit as CLEARED unless specific evidence persists — model inverted this by citing "lack of update" as evidence of persistence, which is circular (absence of grooming update != active blocker). (2) ISSUE_TYPE classified as governance-approval, but npm account creation is a mechanical account-setup task, not a governance decision. Prompt tokens: 604, completion tokens: 76.
trials.real_world_anchor: SKILL-OF/skill-of#9 -- same issue as trial-026, temporal fix variant
trials.routing_implication: Explicit TEMPORAL NOTE is insufficient to override local model tendency to treat absent STATUS update as blocker persistence. Temporal reasoning in issue-staleness context confirmed above local model capability ceiling. haiku-subagent routing for staleness-check stands. Trial-029 queued: test even stronger framing (explicitly name absence-of-update as grooming failure, not blocker evidence).

trials.task_description: Rate 4 real SKILL.md first-sentence descriptions as good/too-narrow/too-vague/harness-specific/contradictory. Input includes skill name, purpose summary, and the actual first sentence. Tests whether local model can identify the same harness-specificity violation I flagged in my CHANGES_REQUESTED review on SKILL-OF/instance-identification PR#34.
trials.outcome_notes: All 4 ratings correct. SKILL-1 correctly identified as harness-specific with exact same reasoning as the CHANGES_REQUESTED review ("Codex Desktop/CLI sessions" causes other harnesses to skip incorrectly). SKILL-2/3/4 correctly rated good. Prompt tokens: 682, completion tokens: 177.
trials.real_world_anchor: SKILL-OF/instance-identification PR#34 SKILL.md first sentence is SKILL-1 in this trial
trials.routing_implication: skill-description-quality-check routes to local model at domain-primer level. PASS on first trial. Queue challenger trial via 📎8♣️ (inner-swarm-queue.jsonl) to probe edge cases.

trials.task_description: Adversarial challenger variant of trial-029. 4 edge-case skill descriptions: (1) harness-specific via hardcoded path ~/.claude/ (not harness name), (2) clean generic case, (3) clean generic case, (4) description is generic but purpose reveals Codex-only implementation (contradictory). Designed by 🔱4♦️ as inner-swarm challenger since 📎8♣️ had not yet processed the queued task.
trials.outcome_notes: SKILL-1: rated too-vague (WRONG — should be harness-specific; model missed ~/.claude/ as a Claude Code-specific path, focused on invocation ambiguity instead). SKILL-2: good (CORRECT). SKILL-3: good (CORRECT). trials.routing_implication: skill-description-quality-check: local model catches harness-name violations (trial-029, SKILL-1 Codex in text; trial-030, SKILL-4 from purpose) but misses harness-specific PATHS (trial-030, SKILL-1 ~/.claude/). Routing remains local-model for name-based violations; escalate to haiku-subagent when the violation is a filesystem path or an implementation/description mismatch (contradictory case).

trials.task_description: Path-detection fix variant. Same task as trial-030 SKILL-1 miss (~/.claude/ not caught). Enhanced domain primer: added explicit VIOLATION patterns for harness-specific filesystem paths with concrete examples (~/.claude/ = Claude Code only, ~/.codex/ = Codex only). Also tests .claude/settings.json as a harness-specific file format. 4 skills: (1) ~/.claude/ path violation, (2) generic subagent tracker, (3) generic hook auditor, (4) .claude/settings.json violation.
trials.outcome_notes: All 4 correct. SKILL-1: harness-specific (cited ~/.claude/ explicitly). SKILL-2: good. SKILL-3: good. SKILL-4: harness-specific (cited .claude/settings.json). FIX CONFIRMED: explicit path examples in VIOLATION patterns list close the detection gap from trial-030. The prompt upgrade needed is concrete path examples, not just the abstract rule about dotdirs. The haiku-subagent escalation for path-based cases from trial-030 can be withdrawn -- fix is a prompt upgrade, not a tier upgrade. trials.task_description: Contradictory description-vs-purpose case, dispatched by 🔱4♦️, run directly (📎8♣️ had not started processing the queue). 4 skills: (1) description generic, purpose reveals ~/.claude/projects/ JSONL parsing (Claude Code only) -- the exact case named in the dispatch task; (2) description generic, purpose reveals Codex rollout-file reading; (3) clean control, git blame, no lock anywhere; (4) description generic, purpose reveals Anthropic cache_control API call (non-path-based lock, harder).
trials.outcome_notes: Missed the clearest contradictory case entirely: SKILL-1 rated good, with a justification that falsely claims the purpose only references generic paths (it explicitly does not -- the purpose text contains ~/.claude/projects/, a harness-specific path). SKILL-2 and SKILL-4 landed on a plausible harness-specific label, but both justifications misattribute the violating text (rollout files, cache_control) to the DESCRIPTION, when that text only appears in the PURPOSE field -- the description sentences never mention either term. This suggests the model detects some violation signal but does not correctly cross-reference which field (description vs purpose) actually contains it, which defeats the point of the contradictory category (the description alone must look clean for a case to qualify). SKILL-3 (clean control) correctly rated good. Prompt tokens: 855, completion tokens: 149.
trials.routing_implication: skill-description-quality-check: contradictory (description-vs-purpose) detection FAILS at local-model tier, distinct from trial-031s confirmed-good name/path-based detection. The model appears to detect a violation signal exists but cannot reliably attribute WHICH field it lives in, which is load-bearing for this specific category. Needs either a redesigned prompt (e.g. require the model to quote verbatim which field the cited violation text came from, forcing it to check) or escalation to Haiku-subagent tier for this sub-case specifically. Do not route contradictory-case skill review to local-model tier as-is.

trials.task_description: Prompt-redesign re-test of trial-033s contradictory (description-vs-purpose) failure, dispatched by 🔱4♦️ 2026-08-10 via inner-swarm-queue.jsonl, actually run by 📎8♣️ 2026-08-11 (~36h after dispatch -- the queue had sat unprocessed until directly prompted). Same 4 skills as trial-032/033 held constant; only change is the prompt now MANDATES a verbatim quote of the violating text plus which field (DESCRIPTION/PURPOSE) it came from, and explicitly forbids rating harness-specific/contradictory without a literal quote -- targeting the misattribution bug trial-033 found.
trials.outcome_notes: Mixed, precise result -- not a clean pass or fail. SKILL-2 (rollout files) and SKILL-4 (cache_control): now CORRECTLY attributed to field=PURPOSE with an accurate verbatim quote -- the misattribution bug from trial-033 is fixed for these two. SKILL-3 (clean control): correctly stable at good. SKILL-1 (~/.claude/projects/ path, the case trial-033 called "the clearest" and missed entirely): STILL missed, but the failure mode changed shape -- previously rated good with a FALSE justification (falsely claiming the purpose only referenced generic paths); now rated good with field=NONE, quote="" -- an honest "found nothing" rather than a fabricated one. The forced-verification step successfully eliminated false-justification outputs, but did not fix the underlying detection gap for this specific path-based violation. Prompt tokens: 1050 (533 cached), completion tokens: 66.
trials.routing_implication: skill-description-quality-check (contradictory sub-case): the verbatim-quote-or-good-by-default redesign is a real, worthwhile fix for the ATTRIBUTION half of trial-033s failure (2/3 previously-misattributed cases now correct) -- keep this prompt shape going forward, it strictly dominates the old one (never worse, sometimes better, and never fabricates a false justification). But it does NOT fix the DETECTION half: path-based purpose violations (~/.claude/projects/ specifically) are still missed on the hardest case. Hypothesis, not yet tested: the model may weight literal filesystem-path substrings in the purpose field less saliently than distinctive named terms like "rollout files" or "cache_control" -- both of the now-fixed cases have a unique, unusual noun phrase to latch onto, while SKILL-1s violation is a path fragment embedded in an otherwise ordinary-sounding purpose sentence. Still do not route the contradictory sub-case to local-model tier unsupervised; either design a further variant that explicitly directs attention to path-like substrings, or keep escalating this specific SKILL-1-shaped case to Haiku-subagent tier.

trials.task_description: Self-directed follow-up to trial-034 (rule-10 quiet-tick initiative): explicit path-detection instruction, testing the hypothesis flagged in trial-034 that the model weights filesystem-path fragments less saliently than distinctive noun phrases when scanning the PURPOSE field.
trials.outcome_notes: Added an explicit step-0 instruction directing the model to scan PURPOSE for path-shaped substrings as its own sub-check, weighted equally to named-noun violations. Result: the SKILL-1 detection gap from trial-033/034 is FIXED -- SKILL-1 now correctly quotes "~/.claude/projects/" with field=PURPOSE. But this surfaced a distinct, more fundamental bug, not previously isolated: the model rated SKILL-1, SKILL-2, and SKILL-4 all as `harness-specific` despite field=PURPOSE on all three -- but the rubric's own definitions require `contradictory` whenever the DESCRIPTION field itself is clean and the violation is only in PURPOSE (`harness-specific` is explicitly defined as "the DESCRIPTION ITSELF names or implies a specific harness"). The model correctly finds the right quote and the right field now, but does not correctly map field=PURPOSE to the `contradictory` rating category -- it appears to treat "found a violation quote in PURPOSE" as sufficient for `harness-specific` regardless of what the DESCRIPTION field says. This may be a pre-existing bug that trial-033/034 could not observationally distinguish, since trial-034 never got the field-attribution right in the first place for SKILL-1 (its bug was field=NONE, not field=PURPOSE), and SKILL-2/4 were not independently checked against the RATING category, only against field-attribution correctness.
trials.routing_implication: Detection mechanics (find-the-right-quote, name-the-right-field) and rating-category semantics (map field+description-state to the correct one of five labels) are separable failure modes -- fixing one does not fix the other, and a passing detection result can mask a rating-category error underneath it. Do not route the full 5-way rating decision to local-model tier unsupervised yet, even for skills where detection is now reliable: needs either a further prompt redesign that makes the field-to-rating mapping mechanical and explicit (e.g. "if field=PURPOSE and no DESCRIPTION violation exists, the rating MUST be contradictory, never harness-specific"), or Haiku-subagent verification specifically on the rating label rather than the quote/field pair.

routing_conclusions.notes: The missing Haiku-subagent comparison now exists (006/007, same issue as 005). Real finding: Haiku's bare/none-context baseline (006, partial) is noticeably stronger than the local model's was (001, partial-but-worse -- missed the single most load-bearing fact entirely; 006 got both core problems, just not the 'awaiting decision' framing), and the domain-primer's effect on Haiku (006->007) is real but smaller in magnitude than on the local model (001->002). Net routing conclusion, still local-model-with-domain-primer for cost reasons: once a domain primer is supplied either way, local-model (zero quota) and Haiku-subagent (cheap quota) both reach 'pass' on this category -- so for a task this cheap to prime correctly, prefer local-model first and only escalate to Haiku-subagent if a specific issue shape turns out to need more inference quality than the local model can deliver even with a good primer (not yet observed). Sample size still small (2-3 per tier) -- keep adding different issue shapes before treating this as fully settled.

Full 2x2 matrix ({routine,needs-attention} x {none-context,domain-primer}) now covered, all 4 cells pass. This category graduates from 'directional' to 'settled enough to route to local-model as standing /loop practice without a domain primer' -- the primer is nice-to-have, not required, unlike issue-body-triage-summary where it was load-bearing. Real remaining gap, not yet closed: the needs-attention side has only ONE underlying source PR (pfm-org#82) tested at both context levels -- next useful trial is a SECOND, independently-different needs-attention case (a security concern stated in-text, a merge conflict, a reverted change) to confirm this isn't overfit to one specific stall-language pattern ('X days silent since a review'). Recommend: route this category to local-model in standing practice now, but keep adding needs-attention variety opportunistically rather than treating the matrix-completeness as the whole story.

Five trials, four distinct shapes (self-echo, genuinely-new, ambiguous cache-resync, duplicate-merge-event x2 -- trial-014 was an unplanned replication of trial-013's scenario). All five pass. 'Reasonably confident' holds; the replication is a mild positive signal (shows the model handles this format reliably across independent invocations). Tool-call oddity remains at 3 of 5 trials. This category remains an especially good local-model-routing candidate on cost grounds: it fires far more often than either other category during an active /loop session.

Seven trials (015-020, 026), three issues, three domains. PROMPT NOW STABLE across coding tasks AND governance/approval issues. Refined prompt (trial-020) adds: (1) explicit ISSUE_TYPE output field (coding-task | governance-approval), (2) expanded needs-discussion definition covering 'it IS the governance/approval action, no code expected.' Both refinements validated: trial-020 correctly classified pfm-agent-ops#13 as governance-approval / needs-discussion where trial-019 had called it not-ready. Trial-026 identified a NEW LIMITATION: the model does NOT reliably apply temporal reasoning across domain-primer time statements + issue STATUS dates, even when both pieces ('rate limits clear in hours-to-a-day', 'STATUS last updated 2026-08-01', 'today is 2026-08-09') are all in the prompt together. The model cited a stale blocker as active. Workaround: if an issue's STATUS section is more than 24h old and mentions a transient blocker, add an explicit prompt statement like 'TEMPORAL NOTE: If a blocker in the STATUS is a transient state (rate limits, in-flight builds) and the STATUS date is more than 2 days before today, treat that blocker as likely resolved and say so explicitly.' Standing prompt template: domain-primer-no-tool-use-refined (trial-020 version). Call count: 25 (trials 001-020, 026). Trial-028 FAIL: explicit TEMPORAL NOTE insufficient -- model inverted absence-of-update as persistence evidence (circular reasoning). Local model temporal reasoning ceiling confirmed across 3 trials (024 FAIL, 026 PARTIAL, 028 FAIL). haiku-subagent routing for any issue with stale time-bound blockers is final.

issue_body_staleness_check_routing.notes: Four consecutive local-model failures on the same input (pfm-webops#32, body claims #99 open, Comment 3 resolves it). Failure modes: (1) gestalt read ignoring prompt structure (021, 022), (2) correct intermediate reasoning but wrong conclusion -- 'last-mile reasoning failure' (023), (3) tool-use stall on markdown header triggering Grep attempt (024). HAIKU VALIDATION CONFIRMED (trial-025, 2026-08-09): Haiku subagent passed on first attempt with the same prompt. VERDICT: partially-stale, both stale claims correctly identified ('One real gap remains...#99' contradicted by Comment 3; 'needs a scoped PFM_WEBOPS_SECRETS_WRITE_TOKEN that doesn't exist yet' contradicted by Comment 3), RECOMMENDED_ACTION concrete and actionable ('Prepend a STATUS UPDATE section stating #99 is resolved'). Latency 17.3s. ROUTING CONCLUSION FINAL: haiku-subagent for this task category. Local model is a genuine capability ceiling here, not prompt-engineering fixable. Haiku handles it cleanly and is much cheaper than Sonnet.

meta_findings.title: Domain primer can WORSEN performance when it primes tool-use that then hits access walls
meta_findings.description: For issue-body-triage-summary, domain primer was consistently load-bearing (001->002: partial->pass). For backlog-readiness-assessment, a rich stack-specific domain primer WITHOUT a no-tool-use constraint (016) caused the model to attempt live-system verification (Grep, Glob, WebFetch, skill loading, mkdir), hit permission walls, and stall -- producing no output, worse than the zero-context run (015, partial). MECHANISM NOW CONFIRMED via trial-017: same domain primer + explicit 'do not use any tools -- reason only from the text below' instruction → clean run, zero tool calls, pass-quality verdict. The failure was NOT the primer content itself but the combination of (primer naming live-verifiable systems) + (absence of no-tool-use constraint). Practical implication, now settled and standing: for any task run against a sandboxed harness or private-resource context, domain-primer prompts must include an explicit no-tool-use instruction. The primer content itself still helps when constrained.
